items.title: Exact Padé coefficient matching with defect statuses
items.statement:
Input nonnegative integers $m,n$ and coefficients $c_0,\ldots,c_{m+n}\in
\mathbb C$ of a formal power series or of an analytic function at $0$. Set
$c_k=0$ for negative $k$. Seek a normalized denominator
$q(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^nq_jz^j$. Form the $n\times n$ moment system
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n}q_jc_{m+\ell-j}=-c_{m+\ell}, \qquad 1\le\ell\le n.$$
Classify it by exact Gaussian elimination on the augmented matrix. Start with
pivot row $r=1$ and scan columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ in order. In column $j$, if
all entries in rows $r$ through $n$ are zero, leave that column free and
continue. Otherwise choose the first row $s\ge r$ with a nonzero entry in
column $j$, swap rows $s$ and $r$, divide row $r$ by its column-$j$ entry,
and subtract the resulting row multiple from every other row to make the
other entries in column $j$ zero; then increment $r$. After all columns, a
row whose coefficient entries are all zero and whose augmented entry is
nonzero makes the system inconsistent, so return status
$\texttt{full-order-inconsistent}$. If the system is consistent but has
rank less than $n$, return status $\texttt{defective-nonunique}$ together
with the rank and reduced system; do not select a denominator from its
affine solution set. Here rank is the number of pivot rows; consistency and rank are
read from the reduced augmented matrix. If the system has rank $n$, return status
$\texttt{full-order-solvable}$ and the unique solution
$(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$ and set
$$p_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,n)}q_jc_{k-j}, \qquad 0\le k\le m,\qquad q_0:=1.$$
The output is the coefficient-matching candidate $p/q$ with its full-order
status. If $n=0$, return status $\texttt{full-order-solvable}$ with the empty
denominator system's unique solution $q=1$ and numerator coefficients
$p_k=c_k$ for $0\le k\le m$.
This procedure claims no pole-location or analytic-continuation guarantee.

references.title: Pedro Gonnet, Stefan Güttel, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Robust Padé Approximation via SVD, Section 2

items.title: Divided differences on distinct nodes
items.statement:
Let $q\ge 0$, let $t_0,\ldots,t_q$ be distinct real numbers, and let $f$ be
real-valued at these nodes. Define the **divided difference** recursively by
$f[t_0]:=f(t_0)$ and, for $q\ge1$,
$$f[t_0,\ldots,t_q]:= \frac{f[t_1,\ldots,t_q]-f[t_0,\ldots,t_{q-1}]}{t_q-t_0}.$$
All sublists in the recursion remain distinct. The denominator is nonzero
because $t_q\ne t_0$, so this recursion gives a finite real number from the
node data.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 5
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Sections 2–3

items.title: A barycentric denominator polynomial with nonzero weights is nonzero

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Section 2
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Section 9.2

items.statement:
Let $k\ge1$, let $z_1,\ldots,z_k\in\mathbb C$ be distinct, and let
$w_1,\ldots,w_k\in\mathbb C$ be nonzero. Then the polynomial
$$
Q(z)=\sum_{j=1}^kw_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell)
$$
is not identically zero.

items.title: Barycentric rational quotient with support values and reduced poles
items.statement:
Let $k\ge1$, let $z_1,\ldots,z_k\in\mathbb C$ be distinct support nodes, let
$f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathbb C$ be data, and let each weight $w_j\in\mathbb C$ be
nonzero. Define the cleared polynomials
$$P(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_jf_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell), \qquad Q(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell).$$
The **barycentric rational quotient** is the rational function $r=P/Q$.
Away from the support nodes this equals
$$r(z)= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_jf_j/(z-z_j)} {\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_j/(z-z_j)}.$$
At a support node its value is given by the cleared quotient $P(z_j)/Q(z_j)$.
A **pole** means a zero of the denominator after all common polynomial
factors of numerator and denominator have been canceled.

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Section 2
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Section 9.2

items.title: Divided differences are symmetric leading coefficients
items.statement:
For distinct real nodes $t_0,\ldots,t_q$ and assigned values $f(t_j)$,
$$f[t_0,\ldots,t_q] =\sum_{j=0}^{q}\frac{f(t_j)}{\prod_{\substack{0\le k\le q\\k\ne j}}(t_j-t_k)}.$$
Consequently the divided difference is symmetric in its nodes. It is the
coefficient of $t^q$ in the unique polynomial of degree at most $q$ that takes
the assigned values at those nodes.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 5
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Sections 2–3

items.title: A solvable Padé moment system gives the stated Taylor order

references.title: Pedro Gonnet, Stefan Güttel, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Robust Padé Approximation via SVD, Section 2

items.statement:
Let $m,n\ge0$, $R>0$, and
$f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty c_kz^k$ for $|z|<R$, with the series convergent
there. Suppose $q_0=1,q_1,\ldots,q_n$ solve the full normalized
Padé moment equations of [[alg-pade-coefficient-matching]]. Define
$p_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,n)}q_jc_{k-j}$ for $0\le k\le m$, and
$p(z)=\sum_{k=0}^mp_kz^k$, $q(z)=\sum_{j=0}^nq_jz^j$. Then
$$
f(z)-\frac{p(z)}{q(z)}=O(z^{m+n+1})\quad\text{as }z\to0.
$$
This is a local Taylor-matching statement only; it gives no pole-location
claim and no guarantee about analytic continuation beyond the neighborhood
where $f$ is given.

Here $h(z)=O(z^M)$ as $z\to0$ means there are constants $C,\delta>0$ such
that $|h(z)|\le C|z|^M$ whenever $0<|z|<\delta$.

items.title: Floater–Hormann barycentric interpolant
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be distinct real nodes, let
$f_0,\ldots,f_n\in\mathbb R$ be data, and let $d$ be an integer with
$0\le d<n$. For $j=0,\ldots,n$, define
$$w_j=(-1)^{j-d} \sum_{i=\max(0,j-d)}^{\min(j,n-d)} \prod_{\substack{i\le k\le i+d\\k\ne j}}|x_j-x_k|^{-1}.$$
The index range is nonempty and every product is positive, so every $w_j$ is
nonzero. The **Floater–Hormann interpolant of degree parameter $d$** is the
barycentric rational quotient of these nodes, data, and weights from
[[def-barycentric-rational-quotient]]. Away from the nodes, exact evaluation
uses the quotient with this denominator;
a zero of the reduced denominator is reported as pole status. The no-real-pole
theorem below proves that this status never occurs for admissible exact real
inputs.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Sections 2 and 4

items.title: Adjacent-window divided-difference recurrence
items.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $n\ge1$, and $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d<n$; let
$x_0<\cdots<x_n$, and let $x$ be distinct from these nodes. For every
$0\le i<n-d$, put
$$G_i:=f[x_i,\ldots,x_{i+d},x].$$
Then
$$G_i-G_{i+1} =-(x_{i+d+1}-x_i)f[x_i,\ldots,x_{i+d+1},x].$$

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, proof of Theorem 2

items.title: Rolle bound for a divided difference

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Theorems 2–3
Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 5

items.statement:
Let $a\le b$, $q\in\mathbb N$, let $f\in C^q([a,b])$, and let $t_0,\ldots,t_q$ be distinct
points of $[a,b]$. Then
$$
|f[t_0,\ldots,t_q]|\le \frac{\|f^{(q)}\|_{\infty,[a,b]}}{q!},
$$
where $0!:=1$, $f^{(0)}:=f$, and
$\|g\|_{\infty,[a,b]}:=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|g(x)|$.

items.title: Hermite–Genocchi simplex formula for divided differences
items.statement:
Let $q\in\mathbb N$, let $f\in C^q([a,b])$, and let
$t_0,\ldots,t_q\in[a,b]$ be distinct real nodes. For $q\ge1$, define
$$\Delta_q=\{(u_1,\ldots,u_q)\in[0,\infty)^q:\ u_1+\cdots+u_q\le1\}, \qquad u_0=1-\sum_{j=1}^q u_j.$$
Then
$$f[t_0,\ldots,t_q] =\int_{\Delta_q}f^{(q)}\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^q u_jt_j\right) \,du_1\cdots du_q, \qquad \operatorname{vol}(\Delta_q)=\frac1{q!}.$$
For $q=0$, the integral is by convention evaluation at $t_0$, and
$\operatorname{vol}(\Delta_0):=1$.
For $q\ge1$, the integral over $\Delta_q$ is the iterated Riemann integral
with $0\le u_1\le1$ and, successively,
$0\le u_j\le1-\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}u_k$ for $2\le j\le q$.

references.title: Carl de Boor, Divided Differences, Section 9, Genocchi–Hermite, pages 63–65, formula (52)

items.title: Barycentric rational quotients are defined and interpolate at support nodes

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Section 2
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Section 9.2

items.statement:
For the data and nonzero weights in [[def-barycentric-rational-quotient]],
$Q$ is not the zero polynomial, the rational function $P/Q$ is well-defined,
and $r(z_j)=f_j$ for each support node $z_j$.

items.title: Finite-sample AAA rational approximation with exact SVD

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Sections 2–4

items.statement:
Input a nonempty ordered list of distinct sample points
$Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\subset\mathbb C$, data
$F=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\in\mathbb C^N$, an absolute tolerance $\tau\ge0$, an
integer support budget $B$ with $0\le B\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, and a finite integer
bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $S\ge0$. The procedure is evaluated in exact
arithmetic; its finite-precision implementation makes no optimality claim.
For $v\in\mathbb C^k$, use the standard Hermitian inner product and Euclidean
norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^k|v_j|^2)^{1/2}$.
Initialize the accepted support-record list $S_{\rm acc}=\varnothing$; each
record stores an original index, its sample point, and its data value. Set the
remaining original-index list $R=(1,\ldots,N)$. Every return has form
$(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\text{status},\mathcal R)$, where $\mathcal R$ is
the residual record maintained below.

1. Set the initial rational candidate $r_0$ to the constant mean
$\bar f=N^{-1}\sum_i f_i$. Compute
$\eta_0=\max_i|f_i-\bar f|$, set the last accepted candidate $r_{\rm acc}=r_0$,
and set $\mathcal R=((0,\eta_0))$. If $\eta_0\le\tau$, return
$(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{tolerance-met},\mathcal R)$.

2. For $m=1,\ldots,B$, choose from $R$ the least original index $s$ that
maximizes the absolute residual from $r_{\rm acc}$. Let $S_{\rm prov}$ be
$S_{\rm acc}$ with $(s,z_s,f_s)$ appended; remove $s$ from $R$.

3. Form the $(N-m)\times m$ Loewner matrix
$L_{ij}=(f_i-f_{s_j})/(z_i-z_{s_j})$, where $i$ ranges over the indices in
$R$ and $s_j$ are the original indices in $S_{\rm prov}$. The denominator is
nonzero because all sample points are distinct.

4. Compute an exact full singular value decomposition (SVD) of $L$ by applying
[[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] followed by
[[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]] with zero deflation
tolerance and budget $S$. If either call returns failure or the QR budget is
exhausted, return $(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{inconclusive},\mathcal R)$.

5. Let $E$ be the right singular subspace for the smallest singular value of
$L$, and let $P_E$ be its orthogonal projection. Choose the least coordinate
index $j$ for which $P_Ee_j\ne0$ and set $w=P_Ee_j/\|P_Ee_j\|_2$. This rule
applies at every multiplicity, including dimension one. Multiply by the
unique unit scalar that makes the first nonzero coordinate of $w$ positive
real. If any coordinate of $w$ is zero, reject this provisional support and
return $(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{zero-support-weight},\mathcal R)$.

6. Form the barycentric rational quotient using the nodes and data in
$S_{\rm prov}$ and $w$ as its weights. If this rational function has a
genuine pole at any remaining sample point, reject this provisional support
and return $(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{pole-status},\mathcal R)$.
Otherwise accept the candidate by setting $r_{\rm acc}$ to it and
$S_{\rm acc}=S_{\rm prov}$, and append $(m,\eta_m,\sigma_m)$, where $\eta_m$
is its maximum sampled residual and $\sigma_m=\|Lw\|_2$, to $\mathcal R$. If
$\eta_m\le\tau$, return
$(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{tolerance-met},\mathcal R)$.

7. If all $B$ iterations finish without another return, return
$(r_{\rm acc},S_{\rm acc},\texttt{support-budget-exhausted},\mathcal R)$. In
particular $B=0$ returns the initial constant and empty support list with this
status when step 1 does not return.

The support tie rule and the projection rule make the exact procedure
deterministic, including when the smallest singular value has multiplicity
greater than one. Rank deficiency is permitted: if the smallest singular
value is zero and all selected weights are nonzero and the quotient is finite
at the remaining sample points, the candidate is accepted and its exact
sample residual is evaluated. The algorithm asserts no uniform off-grid error
bound and no minimax optimality. The Loewner residual $\sigma_m$ is a linear
least-squares residual, not the nonlinear sampled residual $\eta_m$.

items.title: Local mesh ratio for degree-zero Floater–Hormann interpolation
items.statement:
For ordered nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_n$, $n\ge1$, set $\beta:=0$ if $n\le2$. If
$n\ge3$, define the **local mesh ratio**
$$\beta= \max_{1\le\alpha\le n-2} \min\left\{ \frac{x_{\alpha+1}-x_\alpha}{x_\alpha-x_{\alpha-1}}, \frac{x_{\alpha+1}-x_\alpha}{x_{\alpha+2}-x_{\alpha+1}} \right\}.$$
All denominators are positive. This parameter is used only for the
degree-zero error bound.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Theorem 3

items.title: Local polynomial in a Floater–Hormann window
items.statement:
For the nodes, data, and degree parameter of
[[def-floater-hormann-interpolant]], let $0\le i\le n-d$. The local
**window polynomial** is
$$p_i(t)=\sum_{k=i}^{i+d}f_k \prod_{\substack{i\le j\le i+d\\j\ne k}} \frac{t-x_j}{x_k-x_j}.$$
All denominators are nonzero because the nodes are distinct. Empty products
equal one, in particular when $d=0$.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Section 2

items.title: Bounded variation controls adjacent Hermite–Genocchi windows
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $0\le d<n$, let $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be real nodes, and fix a real query point
$x\in[x_0,x_n]$ distinct from the nodes. Let $f\in C^{d+1}([x_0,x_n])$, put
$g=f^{(d+1)}$, and suppose $g$ has finite total variation
$V=\operatorname{Var}_{[x_0,x_n]}(g)$ as defined in
[[def-bounded-variation-and-total-variation]]. For $0\le i\le n-d$, put
$G_i=f[x_i,\ldots,x_{i+d},x]$. Then
$$\sum_{i=0}^{n-d-1}|G_{i+1}-G_i|\le \frac{V}{(d+1)!}.$$

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Sections 2–3

items.title: A global mesh ratio bounds the local degree-zero ratio

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Theorem 3

items.statement:
Let $x_0<\cdots<x_n$, $n\ge1$, put
$h=\max_{0\le j<n}(x_{j+1}-x_j)$ and
$h_{\min}=\min_{0\le j<n}(x_{j+1}-x_j)$, and let
$\rho=h/h_{\min}$. The local ratio $\beta$ in
[[def-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio]] satisfies $0\le\beta\le\rho$.

items.title: Floater–Hormann window polynomials interpolate their local data

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Section 2

items.statement:
For each window $i$, the polynomial $p_i$ in
[[def-floater-hormann-window-polynomial]] has degree at most $d$ and satisfies
$p_i(x_k)=f_k$ for every $i\le k\le i+d$. It is the unique polynomial of
degree at most $d$ with those values. In particular, when all local data
equal $1$, the local Lagrange basis functions sum to the constant polynomial
$1$.

items.title: AAA weights minimize the Loewner residual and interpolate support data

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Sections 2–4
Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, fourth edition, singular value decomposition

items.statement:
At an AAA iteration whose exact SVD call completes successfully, with Loewner matrix
$L\in\mathbb C^{(N-m)\times m}$,
the selected unit weight vector $w$ minimizes $\|Lv\|_2$ among all
$v\in\mathbb C^m$ with $\|v\|_2=1$; its residual is the smallest singular
value of $L$. If every selected weight is nonzero and the iteration does not
return pole status, its barycentric candidate interpolates all selected
support data. The finite support budget makes the procedure terminate after
at most $B$ iterations. These claims concern finite sampled data and do not
assert minimax optimality or uniform off-grid convergence.

items.title: Floater–Hormann weights equal the local-polynomial blend weights
items.statement:
For $n\ge1$ and $0\le d<n$, define
$$\lambda_i(x)=\frac{(-1)^i}{\prod_{k=i}^{i+d}(x-x_k)},\qquad \mu_i(x)=\prod_{j<i}(x-x_j)\prod_{k>i+d}(x_k-x), \qquad 0\le i\le n-d,$$
where empty products equal $1$. Put $s(x)=\sum_i\mu_i(x)$ and let $p_i$ be
the window polynomials in [[def-floater-hormann-window-polynomial]]. For
$x\notin\{x_0,\ldots,x_n\}$, the Floater–Hormann quotient is
$$r_d(x)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i(x)p_i(x)}{\sum_i\lambda_i(x)} =\frac{\sum_i\mu_i(x)p_i(x)}{s(x)}.$$
Moreover, clearing the node factors in the barycentric denominator gives
$\prod_{j=0}^n(x-x_j)\sum_i\lambda_i(x)=(-1)^{n-d}s(x)$.
After clearing and canceling the displayed factors, this is a polynomial
identity valid at every real $x$, including the nodes.
Expanding this expression into a support-node barycentric quotient gives
exactly the weights in [[def-floater-hormann-interpolant]]. Its continuous
values at the nodes are the assigned data.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Sections 2 and 4
Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation, Section 9.2

items.title: Newton remainder for a Floater–Hormann window polynomial
items.statement:
Let $x\notin\{x_i,\ldots,x_{i+d}\}$. For any real data at these nodes and at
$x$, the local polynomial from
[[def-floater-hormann-window-polynomial]] satisfies
$$f(x)-p_i(x)= \left(\prod_{k=i}^{i+d}(x-x_k)\right) f[x_i,\ldots,x_{i+d},x].$$

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, proof of Theorem 2

items.title: Floater–Hormann blend partial sums are positive in each node gap
items.statement:
Let $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ and $0\le d<n$, and use the $\mu_i$ and
$s=\sum_{i=0}^{n-d}\mu_i$ of
[[lem-floater-hormann-weight-and-blend-identity]]. For
$x_\alpha<x<x_{\alpha+1}$, partition the indices into
$$I_1=\{i\le\alpha-d\},\quad I_2=\{\alpha-d+1\le i\le\alpha\},\quad I_3=\{i\ge\alpha+1\},$$
intersecting each set with $\{0,\ldots,n-d\}$. Each nonempty partial sum
$\sum_{i\in I_k}\mu_i(x)$ is positive. More precisely, if $I_3$ is nonempty,
its terms alternate starting positive with strictly decreasing magnitudes; if
$I_1$ is nonempty, its terms have the same property when read backward from
$i=\alpha-d$. If $d\ge1$, every term in $I_2$ is positive.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, proof of Theorem 1

items.title: Floater–Hormann barycentric denominator lower bound
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $0\le d<n$, $x_0<\cdots<x_n$, and
$h=\max_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)$. Let $D_d(x)=\sum_{j=0}^n w_j/(x-x_j)$ be the
Floater–Hormann denominator from
[[def-floater-hormann-interpolant]]. For every open gap
$x_\alpha<x<x_{\alpha+1}$,
$$|D_d(x)|\ge \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{d!\,h^{d+1}}, & d\ge1,\\[4pt] \dfrac{1}{h(1+\beta)}, & d=0, \end{cases}$$
where $\beta$ is the local ratio of
[[def-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio]].

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, proofs of Theorems 2–3

items.title: Floater–Hormann interpolants have no real poles

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Theorem 1

items.statement:
For any $n\ge1$, any distinct ordered real nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_n$, any real
data $f_0,\ldots,f_n$, and any integer $0\le d<n$, the exact
Floater–Hormann rational function in
[[def-floater-hormann-interpolant]] has no real poles.

items.title: Uniform meshes refute the C^(d+1)-seminorm-only Floater–Hormann rate
items.statement:
The refuted claim is that, for every integer $d\ge0$ and $\rho\ge1$, there
exists a constant $C(d,\rho)$ such that for every $n>d$, every ordered
distinct real mesh $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ in a compact interval $[a,b]$, and every
$f\in C^{d+1}([a,b])$, the exact Floater–Hormann interpolant $r_d$ satisfies
the following bound whenever $h/h_{\min}\le\rho$, where
$h=\max_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)$ and $h_{\min}=\min_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)$:
$$\|f-r_d\|_\infty\le C(d,\rho)h^{d+1}\|f^{(d+1)}\|_\infty$$
Here $\|q\|_\infty:=\sup_{t\in[a,b]}|q(t)|$ for continuous $q$ on $[a,b]$.

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Sections 2 and 4

items.title: Floater–Hormann error bounds for a bounded-variation highest derivative
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $0\le d<n$, and $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be real nodes in
$[a,b]=[x_0,x_n]$. Put
$h=\max_{0\le j<n}(x_{j+1}-x_j)$, $m=n-d$, and
$\epsilon=1$ if $m$ is even and $\epsilon=0$ if $m$ is odd. Let
$f\in C^{d+1}([a,b])$, set $g=f^{(d+1)}$, and suppose $g$ has finite total
variation $V=\operatorname{Var}_{[a,b]}(g)$ as defined in
[[def-bounded-variation-and-total-variation]]. For a continuous $q$ on
$[a,b]$, write $\|q\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|q(x)|$. If $d\ge1$, then
$$\|f-r_d\|_\infty \le \frac{h^{d+1}}{d+1}\bigl(V+\epsilon\|g\|_\infty\bigr),$$
If $d=0$, let $\beta$ be the local mesh ratio in
[[def-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio]]. Then
$$\|f-r_0\|_\infty\le h(1+\beta)\bigl(V+\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty\bigr).$$
No mesh-ratio restriction is needed when $d\ge1$. For $d=0$, a fixed global
mesh-ratio bound $\rho=h/h_{\min}$ implies $\beta\le\rho$ by
[[lem-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio-bounded-by-global]].

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Sections 2–3

items.title: Floater–Hormann C^(d+2) parity error bounds
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $0\le d<n$, and $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be real nodes in
$[a,b]=[x_0,x_n]$. Put
$h=\max_{0\le j<n}(x_{j+1}-x_j)$, $m=n-d$, and
$\epsilon=1$ if $m$ is even and $\epsilon=0$ if $m$ is odd. Let
$f\in C^{d+2}([a,b])$ and let $r_d$ be the exact Floater–Hormann interpolant.
For a continuous $q$ on $[a,b]$, write
$\|q\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|q(x)|$. If $d\ge1$, then
$$\|f-r_d\|_\infty \le h^{d+1}\left( \frac{(b-a)\|f^{(d+2)}\|_\infty}{d+2} +\epsilon\frac{\|f^{(d+1)}\|_\infty}{d+1} \right).$$
If $d=0$, let $\beta$ be the local mesh ratio in
[[def-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio]]. Then
$$\|f-r_0\|_\infty \le h(1+\beta)\left( \frac{(b-a)\|f''\|_\infty}{2} +\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty \right).$$
No quasi-uniformity hypothesis is needed when $d\ge1$. If $d=0$, a bound
$\beta\le\rho$ follows from a global mesh-ratio bound $\rho$ by
[[lem-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio-bounded-by-global]].

references.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation, Theorems 2–3

title: Barycentric rational and aaa approximation — Examples

items.title: Padé matching can be singular or create a Froissart doublet

references.title: Pedro Gonnet, Stefan Güttel, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Robust Padé Approximation via SVD, Sections 2 and 5

items.statement:
This example exhibits a rank-deficient normalized moment system, an
inconsistent full-order system, and a Padé pole-zero pair for an entire
polynomial target. It shows why coefficient matching alone supplies no
pole-location or analytic-continuation guarantee. A close pole-zero pair with
small residue is called a Froissart doublet.

items.title: Zero AAA sample residual can coexist with arbitrary off-grid error

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Sections 3–4

items.statement:
Let the sample set be $Z=(0,1)$ and, for any $M>0$, let
$f_M(t)=Mt(1-t)$ on $[0,1]$. Exact AAA with support budget $B=1$, sweep
budget $S=0$, and tolerance zero starts at the constant mean of the two
samples and returns immediately with zero sampled residual, but its uniform
error is $M/4$.
For a continuous $q$ on $[0,1]$, write
$\|q\|_{\infty,[0,1]}:=\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|q(t)|$.

items.title: AAA recovers a scalar transfer-function pole from four samples

references.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation, Sections 2–4

items.statement:
The scalar transfer function $H(z)=C(zI-A)^{-1}B$ with $A=[2]$ and
$B=C=[1]$ is $H(z)=1/(z-2)$. On the ordered sample set
$Z=(0,1,3,4)$, exact AAA with support budget $B_{\max}=2$, tolerance $0$,
and bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $S=1$ selects support nodes $1$ and $3$ and
returns the exact transfer function. Its reduced denominator has the true
pole $z=2$.
